MakeO, the parent company of clear aligner brand Toothsi, has raised Rs 90 crore (approximately $9.4 million) in a funding round led by Singularity AMC. **DSP family office, Genesis and Unispace Ventures also participated in the round.**

The Mumbai-based dental and personal care startup plans to use the fresh capital to expand its offline footprint across India and Southeast Asia, strengthen manufacturing operations and invest in consumer experience, clinical centres and backend technology. **The company is also evaluating acquisitions of dental clinic chains and aligner businesses across the two regions to accelerate its offline expansion.**

**The fundraise follows MakeO's acquisition of Singapore-headquartered Zenyum, for which it announced an agreement in February.** The deal expanded the company's presence in Southeast Asia and strengthened its regional operations.

Following the Zenyum acquisition, the combined business has a network of around 1,100 partner dentists across 10 countries. According to the company, it also operates more than 60 offline clinical centres and has served over 4 lakh consumers.

**Founded in 2018 by Arpi Mehta, Pravin Shetty, Manjul Jain and Anirudh Kal, MakeO initially entered the market with Toothsi, its clear aligner brand.** In 2022, the company brought Toothsi and Skinnsi under the MakeO umbrella to offer dental, skin and hair treatments through a single platform.

**Before the latest funding round, MakeO had raised more than $100 million from investors including Eight Roads Ventures, 360 ONE Asset and Paramark Ventures.** Its previous fundraises included Rs 100 crore in June 2025 and a $16 million round led by 360 ONE Asset and the investment office of Ashish Kacholia in January 2024.

![{Funding Alert} Bengaluru Home-Furnishing Startup wudhomes Raises Rs 2.5 Cr](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-13T114450.121.jpg)

wudhomes, a Bengaluru-based home-furnishing startup founded by Vasu Arneja and Aditya Singh, has raised Rs 2.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by AJVC, founded by Aviral Bhatnagar. **Seekho co-founders Rohit Choudhary, Keertay Agarwal and Yash Banwani, along with other angel investors, also participated in the round.**

The company will use the funds to develop a vertically integrated supply chain, build in-house technology, strengthen its retail experience, and expand its operational capabilities. **The investment will support its efforts to connect different stages of the home-furnishing journey, from product discovery and design selection to delivery and fulfilment.**

wudhomes aims to address the challenges consumers face when turning home-design inspiration into functional living spaces. Customers often rely on social media, design platforms and showrooms for ideas, but selecting furniture, coordinating products, managing budgets and arranging deliveries across multiple vendors can make the process complex.

**To address this gap, the startup is developing an integrated model combining digital inspiration, personalised product curation, spatial visualisation, physical retail, home visits and supply-chain management.**

**In recent months, wudhomes has furnished over 200 homes.** It has also opened a retail outlet on Sarjapur Road in Bengaluru and introduced a home-visit service, through which consultants assess customers' spaces and recommend suitable furnishing options. These initiatives are designed to connect online product discovery with in-person assistance and fulfilment.

> “We believe there is an opportunity to build a much larger business around home furnishing than traditional retail has allowed for. Today, customers have to navigate multiple platforms, stores and vendors to bring their homes together. At wudhomes, we're building a model that brings together inspiration, design, technology, physical retail and an integrated supply chain into one connected journey, with the potential to change how the category works and how it scales,” **said Vasu Arneja, Co-founder, wudhomes.**

> **Aviral Bhatnagar of AJVC shared**, “wudhomes is approaching home furnishing as an end-to-end customer experience rather than just a product category. By bringing together digital discovery, curation and visualisation with physical retail and home visits, the team is addressing the gap between finding inspiration and actually creating a home. We believe this integrated model has the potential to build a differentiated business in a large, underserved market.”

> **Aditya Singh, Co-founder, wudhomes added,** “There's a significant gap between knowing how you want your home to look and actually making it happen. We want wudhomes to bridge that gap, helping customers move from inspiration and design choices to products that fit their spaces and are delivered to their homes. Building the technology and operational capabilities behind this journey is central to how we see the business evolving.”

**The company plans to expand beyond furniture over time. It has not disclosed its valuation, revenue or expansion timeline.**

D2C fitness and sportswear brand Boldfit has raised around Rs 400 crore (approximately $41.8 million) from Bharat Value Fund as part of its Series B funding round. **The fund is a Category II Alternative Investment Fund managed by The Wealth Company Alternates, which is part of Pantomath Group.**

**The Bengaluru-based company plans to use the fresh capital to expand its retail presence across India, invest in product innovation and strengthen its manufacturing capabilities**. Boldfit also intends to explore selective acquisitions to expand its presence and capabilities across product categories.

Founded in 2018 by Pallav Bihani, Boldfit offers performance sportswear, athletic footwear, sports equipment, and fitness essentials. The company claims to serve more than 2 crore customers annually across India.

![Hygiene Brand Niine Targets Rs 1,000 Cr Revenue With Five-Year Growth Plan](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-12T180757.069.jpg)

Niine, an Indian hygiene brand, has set a target of achieving more than Rs 1,000 crore in revenue by FY30 as part of a five-year growth strategy focused on manufacturing expansion, wider distribution, and portfolio diversification. **Founded in 2018 with sanitary napkins, the company has expanded into baby care and plans to address hygiene needs across different stages of life.**

**As part of its roadmap, Niine has invested more than Rs 100 crore in expanding its Gorakhpur manufacturing facility in Uttar Pradesh, with further investments planned to support future growth.** The company aims to extend its general trade coverage to all states, up from its current presence in more than 18 states, while strengthening distribution across modern trade, general trade, and e-commerce. **It also plans to increase its reach in metropolitan areas and Tier 2 markets through strategic partnerships and a broader hygiene portfolio.**

**Niine recorded revenue of Rs 32.46 crore in FY19, its first full year of sales after launching in May 2018.** Revenue increased to Rs 325 crore by FY26, representing 10-fold growth. The company also became EBITDA-positive in FY26 and is targeting an EBITDA margin of 15 percent by FY30. **Its Gorakhpur facility, classified under Uttar Pradesh's super mega industrial category, has created more than 1,000 direct jobs.**

**Product innovation and menstrual hygiene awareness remain part of the company's strategy.** Niine introduced resealable sanitary napkin packs and biodegradable disposal bags, while its vending machine initiatives across educational institutions and public facilities aim to improve access to menstrual hygiene products.

**The brand has also undertaken awareness campaigns, including #LetsTalkPeriods and a partnership with Rajasthan Royals, to encourage conversations about menstruation and involve men in menstrual hygiene awareness.** Its Niine Movement and Run4Niine initiatives have further supported these efforts. In May 2026, the company marked Menstrual Hygiene Day with a digital film series highlighting the different experiences and needs of consumers during menstruation.

> **Amar Tulsiyan, Founder, Niine, said**, "We learnt that the categories people find hardest to discuss are often the ones most in need of a better product. That’s why we started a conversation nobody wanted to have with our ‘Let’s Talk Periods’ campaign. Niine will continue to step into hygiene spaces that are not explored enough. Our Rs 1,000 crore ambition reflects the scale of the opportunity ahead, and we intend to achieve it by reaching many more Indian homes with a portfolio that caters to every stage of life."

The company plans to build on its manufacturing investments and distribution network to expand its presence in India's hygiene market and reach more households through its growing product portfolio.

Medical cannabis wellness startup Awshad has reported that consumers aged 30–40 account for approximately 44 percent of its customers with known age data, making them its largest consumer segment. **As the company completes five years of operations, its data indicates growing interest in wellness products among working-age Indians, with consumers aged 20–30 emerging as its second-largest customer group.**

**Anxiety and sleep-related products are among the largest categories in Awshad's portfolio, reflecting consumer interest in stress management, mental wellbeing and sleep support.**

**The trend comes amid growth in India's health and wellness market.** The market was valued at approximately $164.35 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach $257.94 billion by 2034. **Awshad's five-year data show that anxiety-related products account for approximately 40 percent of its orders, while insomnia and sleep-related products contribute around 20 percent.** Together, these categories represent approximately 60 percent of the company's total order volume.

**The startup has recorded more than 12,000 orders across over 1,400 cities, covering all 36 states and Union Territories.** Its data also indicates differences in purchasing patterns across age groups, with older consumers contributing a more significant share of demand in categories such as chronic pain management.

> **Richa Jaggi, Co-founder, Awshad shared, "**What stands out from our five-year data is how strongly wellness is becoming part of the everyday consumer conversation nowadays, particularly among working-age consumers. The consumer today is more aware, more willing to explore different wellness options, and increasingly looking at wellbeing as part of a regular lifestyle rather than an occasional consideration.”

> **Shivam Singhee, CEO, Awshad, said,** “For the industry, this shift represents a larger opportunity but also a responsibility to build consumer trust as the category grows. Consumers are looking beyond simply discovering new products. They want transparency, consistency, and credible information before making wellness part of their regular choices.”

**With its customer base spread across more than 1,400 cities, Awshad sees an opportunity to expand its reach as wellness products gain traction through digital commerce and mainstream retail.** The company believes that understanding consumer demographics, product preferences, and repeat purchasing behaviour will become increasingly important for brands operating in India's growing wellness market.

> “We are learning retail right now. We’ve had very good positive early signs for us. The idea is that we are using this money to create our playbooks, and then the retail expansion is something which should be funded by franchisees,” **shared Yash Sarawagi, cofounder, KISAH.**

Before this round, **KISAH had raised approximately Rs 10 crore from angel investors, including Sagar Daryani, founder of Wow! Momo, and Apoor Salarpuria of the Salarpuria Group.**

**Founded in 2018 by Sarawagi, KISAH initially operated as a marketplace-led business before expanding through its direct-to-consumer (D2C) platform and physical stores.** His sister, Yashwi Ladsaria, later joined as co-founder, followed by Saurav Kothari. The brand sells through online platforms such as Myntra, Amazon, AJIO, and Nykaa.

**KISAH offers contemporary ethnicwear and occasionwear for men and children, targeting wedding guests and consumers beyond the traditional groom segment.** Its portfolio includes kurtas and sherwanis alongside modern styles such as bomber jackets, flared trousers and sneakers. According to Sarawagi, its products sell at an average price of around Rs 4,000 on Myntra, compared with approximately Rs 1,000 for the platform's overall ethnicwear category.

**The brand began its offline expansion with a store in Kolkata's Gariahat in 2025, generating Rs 45-50 lakh during its first partial year before reaching annual sales of around Rs 70 lakh.** It subsequently opened a flagship store in Bengaluru's Indiranagar in September 2025 and another at Hyderabad's Sarath City in November 2025.

KISAH currently operates 12 stores across markets including Bengaluru, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Mumbai and Visakhapatnam. **It plans to expand further in Bengaluru and explore markets such as Jaipur and Visakhapatnam.**

**The company aims to reach approximately 100 stores and Rs 500 crore in revenue before entering broader categories.** Over the next 12-18 months, it also plans to integrate its online and offline operations to strengthen its omnichannel shopping experience.

![{Funding Alert} EV Charging Startup Ionage Raises $1.3 Mn in Funding](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-12T115158.127.jpg)

Electric vehicle (EV) charging and energy management platform Ionage has raised $1.3 million in a pre-Series A funding round from strategic investors and a consortium of senior executives from global energy and infrastructure companies. **The startup will use the funds to expand its coverage across India's active EV charging networks, improve charger discovery and payment services, and help small and medium-sized charge point operators (CPOs) establish and manage charging stations.**

**Ionage currently supports more than 25,000 four-wheeler charging points, 63 fleets and 75 charging partners across 33 states and Union Territories, covering nearly 3,000 cities.** The company also claims its platform operates on more than 70 percent of India's charging hardware, connecting with major EV charger manufacturers during installation.

**The funding comes amid challenges in India's expanding EV charging ecosystem, including unreliable public chargers and limited integration between different networks.** Ionage estimates that nearly two in five public chargers are non-functional at any given time. It also cited a ratio of one charger for every 235 EVs in 2025.

To address these gaps, the company provides a software and interoperability platform connecting charging operators, original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), property owners, and EV drivers. Its solutions enable users to discover charging stations, access services, and make payments across networks without relying on separate applications for individual operators.

> “We’re building the layer that fixes that: the operating system every charger can run on, whoever owns it, so that discoverability and reliability stop being the exception and start being the default,” **said Vimal Kumar V, co-founder and CEO, Ionage.**

**The company's product portfolio includes Nexus, a charging network management platform for operators, and the IONAGE App, which helps drivers locate chargers, plan routes and make payments.** It also operates Flo, a marketplace connecting charging operators with fleet operators, and CASA, a home charging and energy management solution currently in beta. Its Discovery API provides real-time charging information to vehicle systems and maps, while its business software development kit is in closed beta.

**Ionage has also begun using artificial intelligence and machine learning for intelligent load balancing and energy trading.** Over the next 18 months, it plans to support charging operator clusters in Tier II cities and help smaller businesses develop charging infrastructure. The startup is targeting monthly energy throughput of at least 20 million units within 12 months, following reported month-on-month growth of 25 percent or more.

Direct-to-consumer (D2C) personal care brand Nat Habit is raising Rs 142.6 crore ($15 million) in a Series C funding round led by Trident Growth Partners, with participation from existing investors Bertelsmann, Firstport, Linklight Ventures and others.

**Nat Habit's board is issuing 22.5 lakh Series C preference shares at Rs 633.5 apiece to raise the capital.**

**Trident Growth Partners is leading the investment with Rs 91 crore, followed by Bertelsmann with Rs 37 crore and Linklight Ventures with Rs 6.8 crore.** Mirabilis, Firstport and Dharmayug Investments will contribute the remaining amount.

**The company will use the fresh capital for business expansion, brand building, general corporate purposes, and other requirements**. Of the total proceeds, Rs 2.6 crore will be allocated towards reducing the employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) pool.

**Nat Habit's post-money valuation stands at approximately Rs 800 crore.**

**Following the fresh share allotment, Trident Growth Partners will hold an 11.44 percent stake in the company, while Bertelsmann's shareholding will stand at 17.54 percent.** Before the latest issue, co-founders Swagatika Das and Gaurav Agarwal each held a 16 percent stake in the business, as per the regulatory filing.

**Nat Habit has also rebranded itself as Breathe Life, signalling a broader positioning beyond its origins as an Ayurvedic personal care brand.** The company offers Ayurvedic personal care products, including shampoos, face washes and moisturisers, and is expanding its positioning towards a wider lifestyle proposition.

The company has yet to file its annual financial statements for FY26. **In FY25, revenue from operations increased 47.2 percent year-on-year to Rs 106 crore. However, its losses rose to Rs 29 crore during the same financial year.**

D2C silver jewellery brand Unniyarcha has raised Rs 10 crore in an early-stage funding round led by Sauce VC, with participation from Consumer Collective Atrium. **The company will use the funds to strengthen its branding and marketing efforts, expand manufacturing and supply chain operations, and introduce new product categories.**

Bengaluru-based cold-pressed oil brand Gramiyaa has secured Rs 18.65 crore in a Series A funding round led by new investor Optiscape Network Holdings. **Existing investors Homegrown Ventures, Campus Fund, and others also participated in the round.**

**The funding follows Gramiyaa's pre-Series A round in March 2025, when the company raised Rs 7.2 crore from Homegrown Ventures, with participation from Campus Fund and Mumbai Angels.**

**Gramiyaa's board has allotted 32,968 Series A compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at Rs 5,657 per share to raise the capital.** Optiscape Network Holdings invested Rs 9 crore, making it the largest contributor to the round. Homegrown Ventures invested Rs 4.5 crore, while Campus Fund contributed Rs 4 crore. Sarya Global Holdings invested Rs 90 lakh, and Rasagna Pulapaka participated with an investment of Rs 25 lakh.

**Gramiyaa's valuation increased by 49 percent to Rs 110 crore in the Series A round, compared with Rs 74 crore during its pre-Series A funding.** The company plans to use the proceeds for growth capital and other general corporate requirements.

Founded in 2016 by Sibi Manivannan, Gramiyaa manufactures cold-pressed oils in-house using traditional oil-making methods. **Its product portfolio includes groundnut, coconut, sesame, and mustard oils, along with virgin coconut and olive oils.**

**The direct-to-consumer (D2C) brand sells through its official website and multiple online retail and quick-commerce platforms, including Amazon, Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart, BigBasket, DMart Ready and FirstClub.**

**Following the latest share allotment, Homegrown Ventures remains Gramiyaa's largest external shareholder, holding a 17.34 percent stake.** Campus Fund holds 9.86 percent, while Optiscape Network Holdings owns an 8.28 percent stake.

**The company's co-founders, Sibi Manivannan, Mohamed Yaseen and Naveenrajaman RL, retain stakes of 26.04 percent, 13.02 percent and 13.02 percent, respectively.**

**Gramiyaa has yet to file its financial results for FY26.** In FY25, the company's revenue grew 72.7 percent year-on-year to Rs 19 crore. However, its losses increased nearly 12.7 times to Rs 4 crore during the same period.

Design-focused lifestyle and technology accessories brand DailyObjects has secured Rs 332 crore (approximately $35 million) in a Series C funding round led by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital, and Axiom Asia Private Capital.

**The funding round, which included both primary and secondary transactions, values the company at around Rs 1,050 crore.** The fresh capital will be used to strengthen the brand’s retail presence, expand product development and research capabilities, enhance brand-building initiatives, and explore opportunities in international markets.

**As part of the transaction, early investor Roots Ventures partially exited its stake in the company, generating an 18X return on its investment.** The firm will continue to remain a shareholder alongside existing investors, including 360 One Asset and Trifecta Capital.

**DailyObjects plans to significantly expand its offline footprint by opening 150 exclusive brand outlets (EBOs) across India over the next five years.** At present, the company operates through nearly 350 retail touchpoints, including its own stores and Apple Premium Reseller locations.

**The company also intends to invest heavily in product innovation, focusing on design, materials, quality enhancement, and research and development across its existing categories.** While DailyObjects initially started as a phone case brand, it has since diversified into technology accessories, workspace essentials, carry products, and lifestyle merchandise.

Founded in 2012 by Pankaj Garg and Saurav Adlakha, DailyObjects has built a portfolio spanning multiple consumer lifestyle categories. **The company said it remains committed to maintaining capital efficiency while pursuing profitable growth through retail and product expansion.**

**With the latest investment, DailyObjects’ total funding raised to date has reached nearly $50 million.** Its investor base includes firms such as Seedfund and 360 One Ventures, with the company’s previous funding round raising $10 million in May 2024.

**Prior to the current round, the company had raised approximately Rs 100 crore in equity capital over the past decade to support business growth and scale operations.**

**Operating revenue increased 31 percent to Rs 110 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 84 crore in FY24.** However, total expenditure also rose by 29.7 percent, reaching Rs 124.5 crore from Rs 96 crore in the previous fiscal year. As a result, losses widened to Rs 16 crore in FY25, up from Rs 10 crore in FY24.

**Looking ahead, DailyObjects has projected revenue between Rs 230 crore and Rs 244 crore in FY26 and is targeting EBITDA profitability.** The company plans to achieve this through growth across its direct-to-consumer channels, exclusive retail stores, airport retail locations, and distribution through more than 250 Apple Premium Reseller outlets.

**In addition to strengthening its domestic presence, DailyObjects is assessing opportunities in overseas markets.** The company is currently in the research and evaluation stage and expects to make more concrete decisions regarding international expansion from the next financial year onward.

Pet nutrition startup TailBlaze Longevity has secured $300,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by US-based venture capital firm Comma Capital. **The company was also recently featured on Bharat Ke Superfounders, further highlighting its presence in India’s growing pet care ecosystem.**

**The newly raised capital will be deployed to launch HeartPour, strengthen its team in Ahmedabad, and broaden its reach among pet parents across the country.** Ahead of the product’s commercial rollout, TailBlaze plans to offer complimentary servings of HeartPour to the first 500 dogs.

Founded in August 2025 by Manaal Maniyar and Palak Devpura, TailBlaze Longevity focuses on canine nutrition and longevity. **The company’s mission is to help dogs live three to five years longer through nutrition plans centered on higher protein and lower carbohydrate formulations.**

**The Ahmedabad-based startup said that HeartPour, its new wet dog food range, is the result of four years of research and development.** The product combines high-protein ingredients and superfoods with an Ayurvedic PanchTatva blend consisting of curcumin, black pepper, parsley, amla, and tulsi.

**In addition to HeartPour, TailBlaze has developed FreshTail, a proprietary technology designed to produce shelf-stable fresh meals.** Its portfolio currently includes more than 200 products, spanning organic dog food, natural treats, grooming products, and pet accessories. **The treats category features ingredients such as coconut, hemp, fish, and strawberry.**

**The startup operates through a WhatsApp-first commerce model while also selling via quick commerce platforms and online marketplaces, including Blinkit and BBNow.**

Similarly, Benny’s Bowl secured $1.4 million in February this year to develop functional pet foods targeting areas such as gut health, allergies, renal health, skin and coat care, and weight management.

Meanwhile, Zoomies Pet Care raised Rs 5 crore in pre-seed funding in March to scale its clean-label, human-grade pet food business**. Larger pet care platforms such as Supertails, which has raised $30 million in Series C funding, are also broadening their offerings across technology-enabled services, personalized pet care, and healthcare solutions.**

![Jewellery Brand QWEEN Bets on Large-Format Stores and Digital Discovery to Drive Growth](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-07T123357.778.jpg)

Jewellery brand QWEEN is aiming to achieve Rs 100 crore in revenue during the current fiscal year as it accelerates its expansion across India through a combination of large-format retail stores, digital discovery, and technology-enabled shopping experiences.

**The brand recently secured backing through a Rs 1,000 crore investment round led by global diamond company Rosy Blue and Japanese luxury jewellery firm Kashikey Co. Ltd.** The funding is expected to support the company’s growth plans over the next two years.

**Founded by Amit Kumar and Suyash Motarwar, QWEEN has opened its first retail outlet in Noida and is preparing to launch additional stores in Delhi and Bengaluru.** The company plans to focus its expansion efforts on Tier I and Tier II cities as it builds a broader national presence.

**QWEEN’s retail strategy centers on large-format jewellery stores exceeding 6,000 square feet, designed to offer consumers a more immersive shopping environment.** The company expects each outlet to achieve operational breakeven within six to eight months of opening.

**The brand currently offers a portfolio of more than 3,000 SKUs spanning plain gold jewellery, diamond jewellery and gemstone collections.** Its assortment includes over 50 gemstone varieties, with products available through both physical stores and digital platforms.

As part of its omnichannel approach, QWEEN is integrating technology into the jewellery-buying journey by connecting online product discovery with in-store experiences. **The company believes digital channels can play a larger role in helping consumers explore products before making purchases at physical locations.**

**After nearly two months of operations, the brand reports an average order value of approximately Rs 1.35 lakh at its offline stores, while online transactions average between Rs 45,000 and Rs 50,000.** According to the company, this gap highlights the importance of experiential retail formats in influencing high-value jewellery purchases, while digital platforms continue to serve as an effective discovery channel.

**QWEEN is positioning itself within the bridge-to-luxury jewellery segment by offering a wide product range alongside a modern retail experience.** The company aims to provide consumers with greater flexibility and control in how they discover, evaluate, and purchase jewellery.

With strong financial backing, a growing store network and a technology-driven omnichannel strategy, QWEEN is looking to build a differentiated presence in India’s jewellery retail market. **The brand’s focus on experiential shopping and digital engagement is expected to play a key role in its expansion across major urban and emerging cities.**

Bengaluru-based healthtech startup Kinetic Age has secured approximately $250,000 in a funding round led by AJVC and Agrasar Ventures. **The company plans to use the fresh capital to strengthen its healthcare offerings and expand its customer base across India.**

The platform brings together multiple healthcare services under a single subscription-based model, including doctor consultations, physiotherapy, fitness training, nutrition guidance, diagnostics, and emotional wellness support. **Through integrated care plans, the company aims to improve adherence to health recommendations by offering ongoing monitoring and assistance.**

**Over the past year, the startup claims to have served more than 600 patients in Bengaluru, delivering over 12,000 healthcare sessions.** The company currently conducts more than 150 sessions daily and reports a monthly retention rate exceeding 70 percent, along with a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of more than 75.

**Kinetic Age has also surpassed Rs 2.5 crore in annual revenue run rate (ARR) as demand for preventive and personalized healthcare services continues to grow.** The company leverages AI-driven care protocols to support treatment planning and patient engagement while working with a network of 25 healthcare providers.

**The startup further stated that referrals contribute significantly to its growth, with nearly one-third of its customers coming through existing user recommendations.** As it expands its healthcare ecosystem, Kinetic Age aims to strengthen its position in India’s growing preventive healthcare and healthy ageing segment.

![{Funding Alert} Sober & Co Raises Rs 75 Lk to Expand Zero-Sugar Mixer Brand Across India](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-07T115044.694.jpg)

Sober & Co, a zero-sugar mixer brand known for beverages sweetened with monk fruit, has secured Rs 75 lakh in a funding round led by Sunaina Bhattacharya and Anuj Dhariwal on behalf of New Ground Collective, a syndicate comprising seven angel investors. The investment values the company at Rs 10 crore.

**The fresh capital will be directed towards increasing inventory levels, enhancing manufacturing capabilities, scaling quick-commerce advertising efforts, and strengthening the team as the brand prepares for broader retail expansion across India.**

**As part of its growth strategy, Sober & Co plans to enter the Pune market by December 2026 and launch on Zepto, adding a second quick-commerce platform alongside its existing presence on Blinkit.** The company also intends to increase marketing investments in Goa over the coming months.

**Founded with a focus on healthier beverage alternatives, Sober & Co offers mixer products sweetened with monk fruit instead of sugar.** The brand currently operates across retail, HoReCa, quick-commerce and direct-to-consumer channels.

**The funding round comes amid strong business growth.** According to the company, its gross merchandise value (GMV) increased by 34.8 percent during the first four months of FY27. On Blinkit, where the brand is available through 400 dark stores, sales have recorded an average monthly growth rate of 37.8 percent. **The company also reported an improvement in CM2 margins from negative 9.09 percent to positive 1.7 percent and achieved breakeven in July.**

**Offline, Sober & Co products are available across 400 HoReCa and retail touchpoints in Kolkata and Goa.**

> **Sunaina Bhattacharya, New Ground Collective said**, “India’s consumers are becoming increasingly health-conscious, while still looking for products that offer great taste and a sense of discovery. Sober & Co. fits naturally into this shift, with exciting, naturally sweetened beverages that don’t compromise on experience. What impressed me equally were Sharaan and Nishaun - their energy, commitment and overall approach to building the brand really stood out. Personally, I love the bold branding, and the products genuinely taste great, they’re almost always stocked at my home. There is genuine customer pull for Sober & Co’s product which is a great start for a brand, and I see strong potential for Sober & Co. to become a leading brand in India’s evolving beverage market."

> **Sharaan Kriplani, Co-founder and CEO, Sober & Co said,** “We’re not chasing every city or every channel at once. We’re building where the category is actually won — HoReCa for credibility, Blinkit for reach, and now D2C to own the customer relationship — and this capital lets us go deeper in Kolkata and Goa before we go wide."

**Looking ahead, the company plans to expand its presence across HoReCa, quick-commerce and D2C channels while strengthening its retail footprint.** Sober & Co intends to replicate its current city expansion model by first establishing distribution through HoReCa and quick-commerce networks before scaling retail operations.

**The brand remains focused on the mixer segment and aims to strengthen its position in India’s growing better-for-you beverage market.** According to industry estimates cited by the company, India’s cocktail mixer market is expected to grow from USD 222.4 million in 2023 to USD 471.53 million by 2032, reflecting a CAGR of 8.69 percent.

The upcoming launch on Zepto is expected to further strengthen Sober & Co’s quick-commerce presence as it expands beyond Blinkit and accelerates its reach among consumers seeking healthier mixer alternatives.

CureMeAbroad, a healthcare technology platform focused on helping patients access treatment options at accredited hospitals overseas, has raised $1.1 million in a pre-seed funding round led by healthcare-focused venture capital firm SteerX Ventures. Existing investor AIRA also participated in the funding round.

**The latest investment comes a few months after the Pune-based startup secured $600,000 in April this year from a group of investors that included Roman Saini, Himanshu Ratnoo, Kunal Gupta, Devaiah Bopanna, Vikrant Potnis, and AIRA.**

According to the company, **the fresh capital will be utilized to expand its network of accredited hospitals, enter new international patient markets, strengthen its AI-powered platform, and scale its technology and operations teams.** The company also plans to diversify beyond elective healthcare services by expanding into specialties such as orthopaedics and oncology. **In addition, CureMeAbroad is exploring the establishment of physical experience centres in key global markets.**

**Founded in June 2025 by Aditya Oza and Mikhail Bohra, CureMeAbroad operates as a healthcare discovery and medical tourism platform that enables patients to compare hospitals, verify healthcare providers, obtain treatment cost estimates, and book medical procedures across multiple countries.**

The platform combines healthcare discovery, treatment planning, transparent pricing, and patient support services into a single ecosystem aimed at simplifying cross-border healthcare decisions. The company currently records more than 22,500 monthly visitors and has established partnerships with hospitals across six countries.

**CureMeAbroad said it is targeting $100 million in annual patient treatment bookings by FY2028, a significant increase from its current run rate of $4.8 million.** The startup’s primary patient acquisition markets include the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia, and Canada, where demand for international treatment options continues to grow.

The company operates in a competitive global medical tourism market alongside platforms such as Bookimed, PlacidWay, The Medical Tourism Company, and Medical Departures. In India, it also competes with medical tourism facilitator Vaidam Health.

**According to the company, it has received Medical Travel Facilitator Certification from Global Healthcare Accreditation (GHA).** Its network currently includes more than 400 accredited hospitals across six countries, enabling patients to access a broad range of treatment options through a verified healthcare ecosystem.

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![{Funding Alert} Kitchen and Bathroom Brand Lorazzo Secures Rs 15 Cr to Fuel Expansion](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-06T155830.243.jpg)

Design-led kitchen and bathroom brand Lorazzo has secured Rs 15 crore in a funding round led by Sauce, with follow-on participation from Sprout Venture Partners. **The round also saw investments from Panthera Peak and Alteria Capital, as the company looks to accelerate its growth in India’s home improvement and sanitaryware market.**

According to the company, the newly raised capital will be deployed towards expanding its product portfolio, strengthening product development capabilities, hiring talent, and enhancing its presence across online and offline sales channels. **The funding will also support Lorazzo’s plans to expand into additional markets across India.**

Founded in 2024 by Jatin Luthra and Saurabh Gupta, Lorazzo operates in the kitchen and bathroom solutions segment, offering a range of products designed to combine functionality, technology, and contemporary design. **The company’s portfolio spans faucets, sinks, shower systems, bidets, wash basins, smart toilets, and other home improvement products.**

**Lorazzo has adopted an omnichannel approach, selling through e-commerce platforms, quick commerce channels, and offline retail networks.** The company aims to modernize traditionally functional home categories by focusing on product innovation, design aesthetics, and consumer convenience.

**Among its flagship offerings is the Intelli Smart Commode, a technology-enabled cleansing WC that features a heated seat, electronically operated bidets, an integrated air dryer, ambient lighting, and digital temperature controls.** The product is priced at Rs 58,999, positioning it as a more affordable alternative to similar international products, which typically range between Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 5 lakh.

The company also differentiates itself through extended product warranties of up to 20 years across select categories, including kitchen sinks, sanitaryware, mirrors, cabinets, and faucets. **In addition, Lorazzo provides installation and after-sales service support across India.**

**The funding comes at a time when demand for premium home improvement products and smart bathroom solutions is gaining momentum in India, driven by rising urbanization, increasing home ownership, and growing consumer interest in design-focused living spaces.**

Lorazzo said it has recorded sixfold revenue growth over the last 12 months and is now targeting Rs 100 crore in revenue over the next two years. The company plans to leverage the fresh capital to deepen its market presence, introduce new products, and strengthen its omnichannel distribution strategy as it scales operations across the country.

![{Funding Alert} SuperMush Secures $3 Mn Funding from NDude Labs to Expand Wellness Portfolio](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-06T120840.274.jpg)

Healthcare and wellness-focused investment firm NDude Labs has announced a $3 million Series A investment in SuperMush, a functional wellness brand known for developing products formulated with research-backed ingredients such as nootropics, adaptogens, and functional mushrooms.

**The funding round, led by NDude Labs, is expected to support SuperMush’s next phase of growth, including product portfolio expansion, investment in advanced formulations, and strengthening the operational infrastructure required to serve a wider customer base.**

**Founded in 2022 by Alli Schaper and Brian Friedman, SuperMush has established a growing presence in the functional wellness segment through an omnichannel retail strategy.** The company currently has products available in more than 2,000 retail stores across the United States, including over 1,000 Target locations and Sprouts, while also maintaining a strong direct-to-consumer and marketplace business.

**Over the past year, the brand expanded its presence to more than 1,000 Target stores and continued to record strong performance through its website and Amazon channels.** It also broadened its product lineup with the introduction of Shilajit, Creatine, and Lion’s Mane gummies as part of its wellness-focused portfolio.

> **Vikram Sehgal, COO at NDude Labs shared,** “NDude Labs invests in differentiated, science-backed products and founders with the vision and grit to build enduring brands. Our investment in SuperMush provides the capital to accelerate the company’s growth, along with the talent, systems and support needed to scale the business thoughtfully and sustainably.”

> **Alli Schaper, Co-founder and CEO, SuperMush** said, “We are so excited to be partnering with NDude Labs for this next phase of our evolution. Over the last few years, we’ve built an incredible community, products and brand presence grounded in our mission to bring the power of functional mushrooms to the world. With their team and capital support, we are preparing to scale our efforts to reach more consumers and build a globally recognized brand.”

> **Brian Friedman, Co-founder, SuperMush stated,** “We're extremely excited to partner with NDude Labs on this next chapter as we evolve SuperMush into the #1 premium functional supplement brand for active lifestyles. With their support, we're going to create the most effective, science-backed supplements using clinically studied ingredients at meaningful doses to help people think better, move better and feel their best.”

The company said it plans to continue building a portfolio centred on scientifically validated ingredients while expanding its presence across retail, direct-to-consumer channels, and online marketplaces. **The strategy is aimed at strengthening its position in the growing functional wellness and dietary supplements market.**

The investment also follows NDude Labs’ recent backing of Nutriventia, a nutraceutical ingredients company, highlighting the firm's continued focus on health and wellness businesses built around science-driven and ingredient-led innovation.

![{Funding Alert} Smart Kitchen Startup Beyond Appliances Secures Rs 110 Cr Funding for Expansion](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-06T112350.901.jpg)

Beyond Appliances, a smart kitchen technology company focused on developing intelligent appliances for Indian households, has raised Rs 110 crore (US$11.4 million) in a Series B funding round led by Fireside Ventures, with participation from Dharana Capital and other investors.

**The Bengaluru-based startup had earlier raised US$4 million in a Series A funding round led by Fireside Ventures, alongside Dharana Capital, in August last year.** Prior to that, it secured US$2 million in seed funding from Fireside Ventures in November 2024.

According to the company, **the fresh capital will be used to accelerate research and development efforts and set up a new manufacturing facility.** The investment is expected to strengthen Beyond Appliances’ capabilities in developing and scaling its next generation of kitchen appliances.

**Founded in 2024 by Eshwar K Vikas and Rakesh Patil, Beyond Appliances develops smart kitchen products that combine technology with everyday functionality for modern homes.**

**The company said it has expanded its product portfolio to include Android chimneys, Plug-N-Play chimneys, smart hobs, and cooktops.** It has also widened its footprint across India while deepening consumer engagement as it continues to grow its operations.

**Beyond Appliances stated that referral-driven sales are contributing significantly to its business, with customer recommendations accounting for 15 percent of its revenue.** Its flagship kitchen appliance range remains the brand’s largest revenue contributor. The company also reported a twofold increase in its marketplace share over the past year, indicating growing consumer demand through online sales channels.

**In addition to its digital presence, the brand operates through offline retail outlets and experience centres in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad.** Looking ahead, Beyond Appliances plans to enter 10 more cities over the next three years. **During the same period, it is targeting an annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 500 crore while maintaining a focused portfolio centred on kitchen appliances.**

**The funding comes at a time when smart kitchen technology is gaining traction within India’s consumer technology and home appliance market.** Rising demand from urban consumers for connected, convenient, and energy-efficient cooking solutions is driving growth in the segment.

**Several startups have attracted investor interest in this category. Upliance.ai, which develops AI-powered cooking appliances, previously raised Rs 34 crore from Khosla Ventures.** More recently, EDT secured US$2.4 million in funding led by Sauce VC, while Curaa raised Rs 40 crore from 3one4 Capital in August this year to expand its kitchen appliances and tools portfolio.

![{Funding Alert} Bangalore Watch Company Plans Global Expansion After $1.4 Mn Seed Raise](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-01T121306.314.jpg)

Indian luxury watchmaker Bangalore Watch Company (BWC) has secured $1.4 million in a seed funding round backed by a group of its customers, including family office principals and high-net-worth individuals from India and international markets.

**The newly raised capital will support the brand’s expansion plans in the global independent watch industry.** BWC intends to strengthen its presence in select international markets known for active watch collector communities while also evaluating opportunities for expansion within India.

Established in 2018 by Nirupesh Joshi and Mercy Amalraj, Bangalore Watch Company designs and manufactures mechanical watches in India and exports its products to more than 30 countries. **The brand is known for creating collections inspired by themes such as aviation, space exploration, cricket, and outdoor adventures, drawing from contemporary Indian narratives.**

**At present, the company operates a flagship boutique in Bengaluru and offers watches priced between Rs 1.5 lakh and Rs 3 lakh.** With an annual production capacity of approximately 1,500 watches, BWC is planning a significant scale-up and aims to increase output fourfold over the next three to five years.

**Over the years, the company has developed several watches using unconventional materials, including aluminium recovered from fighter aircraft and materials sourced from aircraft carriers.** It has also introduced its proprietary Cerasteel material and created a watch that qualified for spaceflight.

**BWC has continued to build visibility within the international watchmaking community through participation in major industry events such as Dubai Watch Week 2025 and Geneva Watch Days 2026.** The brand’s watches have also been shortlisted for the Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève (GPHG) Awards on three occasions.

The latest funding is expected to help Bangalore Watch Company strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, expand its international reach, and further establish itself in the growing global market for independent luxury watch brands.

 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

![{Funding Alert} Healthtech Startup Aignosis Bags Rs 4 Cr to Scale Early Childhood Screening Platform ](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-10/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-10-01T115001.772.jpg)

Jaipur-based healthtech startup Aignosis has secured Rs 4 crore in a seed funding round led by Antler, Nikhil Kamath, and a group of angel investors, including Varun Dua and IIMA Ventures.

**The newly raised capital will be used to strengthen the company's AI-powered autism and developmental screening platform and expand its reach across India.**

**Founded by Raksheet Jain and Divyansh Mangal, Aignosis previously raised its first funding round in 2024 from investors such as Rajneesh Bhandari and Amit Jain.** The startup has since completed the CDSCO regulatory process and obtained Class B certification. **It was also selected as part of the Google for Startups Accelerator: AI First 2025 cohort.**

**Aignosis has developed an AI-assisted screening solution designed for children between 16 months and nine years of age.** Using a standard laptop and webcam, the platform records a short video session consisting of nine stimulus-based modules. **The system then applies computer vision technology to evaluate behavioural indicators, including gaze patterns, response to name, and reactions to facial expressions.**

**Based on the analysis, the platform generates a risk assessment report that highlights whether a child may require further clinical evaluation.** The company clarifies that the tool is intended for screening purposes and does not provide a medical diagnosis.

**The startup currently follows a Clinic-in-Clinic deployment model and has rolled out its solution across more than 20 government Primary Health Centres in Rajasthan.** It has also entered into a partnership with Mankind Pharma, where the pharmaceutical company's medical representatives support screening camps conducted alongside paediatricians in different parts of the country.

In addition, **Aignosis has begun working with Apollo Shines and is set to introduce its screening services across approximately 125 schools.**

**According to the company, it has conducted over 8,000 screenings to date and is targeting at least 1 lakh screenings by the end of FY27.**

Looking ahead, Aignosis plans to expand its presence into Punjab, NCR, Haryana, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Karnataka, and Maharashtra.

![{Funding Alert} Home Interior Materials Startup Gravity Secures $15 Mn Funding](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-30T185111.811.jpg)

Bengaluru-based home interior materials startup Gravity has secured $15 million in a combination of equity and debt funding. **The investment round was led by Info Edge Ventures and 3one4 Capital, with participation from Alteria Capital, Genesia Ventures, and several angel investors.**

**Founded by former Livspace executives Saurabh Jain and Lalit Mittal, Gravity is developing a technology-driven platform focused on India’s home interior materials sector.** The company currently operates in the kitchen and wardrobe categories, bringing together specialist businesses through a shared ecosystem of technology, distribution, key account management, and operational infrastructure.

**The businesses within its initial portfolio collectively generate revenues in the multi-hundred-crore range and are EBITDA positive.**

**With the fresh capital, Gravity plans to strengthen its technology capabilities, expand its distribution network, and enhance its key account management infrastructure.** The startup also intends to invest in category expansion, brand development, and working capital requirements.

As part of its growth strategy, the company is looking to broaden its presence beyond kitchens and wardrobes by entering adjacent home interior categories, including doors and windows, lighting solutions, wall surfaces, home automation, and other interior systems.

**Prior to launching Gravity, Saurabh Jain served as Chief Executive Officer of Livspace India, where he played a key role in scaling the company to an annualized revenue run rate of approximately Rs 1,500 crore.** Co-founder Lalit Mittal previously held the position of Chief Business Officer for India and led Livspace’s expansion into more than 30 cities.

Gravity’s platform is designed to cater to architects, interior designers, modular showroom operators, and design-and-build firms that play a significant role in specifying and procuring materials for residential interior projects.

**The company aims to streamline sourcing processes across a fragmented supplier ecosystem while improving product availability, fulfillment efficiency, and pricing transparency for industry stakeholders.**

![{Funding Alert} EV Startup Simple Energy Secures Rs 1,750 Cr to Accelerate Growth](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-30T171853.569.jpg)

Electric two-wheeler manufacturer Simple Energy has secured Rs 1,750 crore (approximately $182 million) in a Series C funding round, marking the largest capital raise in the company’s history. **The round also ranks among the biggest funding deals secured by an Indian electric two-wheeler original equipment manufacturer (OEM).**

**The investment round was led by the family office of Dr. Arokiaswamy Velumani, founder of Thyrocare Technologies**. Existing stakeholders, including founder and Chief Executive Officer Suhas Rajkumar and co-founder and Chief Financial Officer Ankit Gupta, also participated in the round. **Bengaluru-based high-net-worth individual (HNI) Amit Mishra and the Haran Family Office joined as investors.**

The company stated that the entire amount was raised through equity financing. Following the latest round, **Simple Energy’s cumulative capital raised has exceeded Rs 2,530 crore (around $263 million).**

**The fresh funding will be deployed to establish a new manufacturing facility, enhance production capacity, strengthen the company’s distribution and service network, recruit talent, and accelerate research and development efforts for upcoming products.** A portion of the capital will also be allocated toward marketing initiatives and supply chain expansion.

**At present, Simple Energy has a manufacturing capacity of 10,000 units per month and operates a network of more than 80 outlets across over 60 cities in India.** Its product lineup includes the Simple One, Simple Wave, and Simple Ultra electric scooters.

**On the financial front, Simple Energy reported operating revenue in the range of Rs 150–160 crore for FY26, compared to approximately Rs 40 crore in FY25.** The growth represents a nearly fourfold increase in annual revenue. The company currently generates a significant share of its sales from southern India.

**Prior to the Series C round, Simple Energy raised Rs 250 crore through a combination of debt and equity financing in June 2026.** In September 2025, the company secured $10 million through an all-equity bridge round. Earlier fundraising efforts included a $20 million Series A round in July 2024, a bridge funding round exceeding $20 million in February 2023, and $21 million in pre-Series A funding in November 2021.

**Founded in 2019 by Suhas Rajkumar and Shreshth Mishra, the company later added Ankit Gupta as a co-founder.** Simple Energy designs and develops electric two-wheelers along with key components such as batteries, motors, chassis, and software platforms in-house.

Doctor-led longevity and preventive healthcare startup Vytalyou has secured Rs 9 crore in a pre-Series A funding round from investors Chetan Jain of Pharma Dose and Ratan Jain of Venus Industries. **The investment values the company at approximately Rs 33 crore.**

According to the company, **the fresh capital will be used to scale its network of Incremental Lifestyle Clinics across Mumbai as it looks to strengthen its presence in the preventive healthcare and longevity segment.**

Founded in 2025 by Chirantan Bose and Preetesh Bhandari, Vytalyou focuses on preventive healthcare solutions and longevity-driven medical services. **The company combines diagnostic assessments with personalized health interventions and medically supervised treatment plans.**

Headquartered in Mumbai, Vytalyou offers a range of services including pathology, radiology, cardio-respiratory evaluations, body composition analysis, genetic and cancer screening, gut microbiome assessments, personalized IV therapies, and regenerative healthcare interventions. **The startup also provides non-invasive pain management solutions for chronic musculoskeletal conditions.**

**The company said it has served nearly 1,000 clients since launching its first centre.** Around 50 percent of its customers have come through direct walk-ins, while the remainder have been acquired through referrals and word-of-mouth recommendations.

**Looking ahead, Vytalyou plans to expand its footprint to 10 locations across India over the coming years as demand for preventive healthcare and wellness-focused services continues to grow.**

**The startup operates in India’s emerging longevity and preventive healthcare market, a segment that has attracted increasing investor interest in recent years.** Several companies in the space have secured funding to support expansion and product development.

**Earlier this year, longevity-focused startup Biopeak raised $2.7 million in follow-on funding.** Cent, co-founded by Practo’s Shashank ND, secured approximately $5 million for its AI-driven early detection platform focused on cancer, cardiac, neurological, and metabolic health risks.

**Meanwhile, Elevate Now raised Rs 18 crore in a seed funding round, while Decode Age secured Rs 14.48 crore in a pre-Series A round to advance its work in longevity research, biomarker discovery, multi-omics, and microbiome science.**

![{Funding Alert} Quick Commerce Fulfilment Startup Blitz Secures Rs 28.7 Cr Funding ](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-30T114406.767.jpg)

Blitz, a startup focused on quick-commerce fulfilment solutions, has raised Rs 28.70 crore in a pre-Series B funding round led by existing investor IvyCap Ventures. 

**The company’s board has approved the issuance of 21,883 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at a price of Rs 13,118 per share to secure the funding.** IvyCap Ventures emerged as the lead investor with a contribution of Rs 12.70 crore. ICMG Group invested Rs 4.75 crore, while Vishal Dhupar participated with Rs 2.50 crore. The remaining capital came from a group of angel investors. 

**The latest investment has pushed Blitz’s post-money valuation to approximately Rs 440 crore, up significantly from Rs 175 crore during its Series A round.** The company is also expected to bring in additional funds as part of the same round, which could further increase its valuation. 

**Blitz intends to use the fresh proceeds to support business expansion, scale operations, and meet general corporate requirements.** The company had previously raised Rs 51 crore in a Series A funding round in November 2024, with IvyCap Ventures leading the investment.

**Established in 2020 by Gaurav Piyush, Mayank Varshney, and Yash Sharma, Blitz provides fulfilment infrastructure for ecommerce and D2C brands, enabling delivery timelines ranging from 10 minutes to 60 minutes, as well as same-day and next-day services.** The startup leverages a network of dark stores and fulfilment centres to accelerate order processing and improve delivery efficiency.

**IvyCap Ventures continues to be the company’s largest external shareholder, holding a 23.47 percent stake.** India Quotient owns 15.31 percent, while AL Trust holds 3.29 percent. ESOPs and MSOPs collectively account for 12.88 percent of the company’s equity. 

**Among the founders, Yash Sharma and Mayank Varshney each own 11.53 percent of the company, while Gaurav Piyush holds a 6.72 percent stake.**

**The shareholder base also includes several well-known angel investors.** Snapdeal co-founders Kunal Bahl and Rohit Bansal hold 0.59 percent each, while QED Innovation Labs and Farid Ahsan, Founder and CEO of General Autonomy, own 0.34 percent each.

**Blitz is yet to submit its FY26 financial statements.** In FY25, the company reported operating revenue of Rs 50.6 crore, compared to Rs 22.18 crore in FY24. During the same period, its losses increased to Rs 24.33 crore from Rs 11.17 crore a year earlier

![{Funding Alert} Pediatric Healthcare Startup Primerry Secures Rs 7.1 Cr in Pre-Seed Round](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-29T152512.204.jpg)

Primerry, a pediatric healthcare startup focused on children’s wellness products, has secured Rs 7.1 crore (approximately $760,000) in a pre-seed funding round. **The investment will support the company’s efforts to develop child-friendly healthcare solutions and expand its presence across India.**

**Founded by Rushabh Nandu and Dr. Nihar Parekh, the round attracted participation from investors including Ashish Kacholia and Lashit Sanghvi, along with angel investors Mohit Sadaani, Hitesh Dhingra, Ajay Mehra, and Samir Palod, as well as select family offices.**

**The newly raised capital will be used to strengthen the company’s research and development capabilities, expand its leadership team, and increase distribution across key markets.**

**Primerry plans to launch its offerings in phases, beginning with a portfolio of eight SKUs priced between Rs 499 and Rs 1,499.** Products will initially be available through the company’s direct-to-consumer platform, while expansion into quick-commerce channels is planned within the first year of operations.

**Alongside its healthcare products, the startup has introduced PocDoc, a customizable carry case designed to help children organize and carry their wellness essentials.** The company aims to encourage regular healthcare habits by combining functionality with a more engaging user experience.

Primerry plans to establish an offline presence through pharmacies, pediatric clinics, and mother-and-baby specialty stores, with an initial focus on metro cities and Tier-I markets.

> **Nihar Parekh, Co-Founder, Primerry expressed,** *"Over years of pediatric practice, we have seen a clear gap in how everyday health needs, such as growth, immunity, gut health, and coughs and colds are managed. We are building clean formulations with unique delivery formats that rebuild parents' trust. The idea is that wellness must be 100 percent trustworthy, meaning there should be absolutely no doubt in the parent's mind, and that kids should actually enjoy it."*

> **Rushabh, Co-Founder, Primerry stated**, *"Every conversation we had with parents revealed a real want for clean, non-medicated solutions. Our goal is to bring the best global formulations and sourcing standards to parents who are increasingly informed and questioning what they buy for their children. We want to build products that balance what children actually need, ease and fun, with what parents care about most: efficacy and convenience ."*

With fresh funding in place, **Primerry is positioning itself to tap into the growing demand for specialized pediatric healthcare products in India,** as parents increasingly seek wellness solutions designed specifically for children's needs.

Aman Gupta, entrepreneur, investor, and co-founder of boAt, has invested in FIG Living, a design-focused home and living brand, through his investment firm SailThru Ventures.

**The investment further strengthens Gupta’s long-standing association with Sushant Sharma, founder of FIG Living, who previously worked alongside him at boAt.**

**Established in 2025, FIG Living initially entered the market with a portfolio of lighting products, including table lamps, portable lamps, pendant lights, wall lights, and floor lamps.** Since then, the company has diversified its offerings to include side tables, accent furniture, and tabletop décor products as part of its strategy to evolve into a broader home and lifestyle brand.

**FIG Living currently operates at an annual revenue run rate of approximately Rs 12 crore and has served more than 40,000 customers.** The brand reported growth of around 20 percent quarter-on-quarter and is aiming to achieve an annual revenue run rate of Rs 18 crore following the upcoming festive season.

**With the fresh investment, FIG Living plans to broaden its distribution reach, enhance offline consumer experiences, and create additional customer engagement touchpoints.** The company is also exploring opportunities for international design collaborations and partnerships as part of its next phase of growth.

**Manufacturing operations are carried out in India through an affiliated facility located in Greater Noida.** Going forward, the brand intends to expand its presence beyond lighting and strengthen its position across multiple home and lifestyle categories.

Electric vehicle manufacturer Zelio E-Mobility has announced plans to raise up to Rs 167.96 crore through a preferential issue of equity shares and convertible warrants as it looks to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities and expand its distribution footprint across India.

**The proposal has been approved by the board of the BSE SME-listed company and remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.** The matter will be placed before shareholders at an Extraordinary General Meeting scheduled for October 20.

As part of the fundraising exercise, **Zelio plans to issue up to 9.73 lakh equity shares at Rs 853 per share to four non-promoter investors, aiming to raise approximately Rs 83 crore.**

**Under the proposed allotment, Motilal Oswal Financial Services will receive 4.70 lakh equity shares valued at around Rs 40.09 crore, while Calliope Capital Advisors LLP is set to receive 3.68 lakh shares worth nearly Rs 31.39 crore.** Param Value Investments will be allotted one lakh shares amounting to Rs 8.53 crore, and Hem Growth Opportunities Fund will receive 35,000 shares valued at approximately Rs 2.99 crore.

**In addition, the board has cleared the issuance of up to 9.96 lakh convertible warrants priced at Rs 853 each to promoters Niraj Arya, Deepak Arya, and Kunal Arya.** The warrant issue is expected to generate up to Rs 84.96 crore.

**According to the company, at least 25 percent of the warrant subscription amount will be paid at or before allotment, with the balance payable upon conversion into equity shares**. The warrants can be converted within 18 months from the date of allotment.

**Following the proposed share issuance and complete conversion of the warrants, promoter and promoter group shareholding is expected to reduce from 72.76 percent to 70.87 percent on a fully diluted basis**. Public shareholding is projected to increase from 27.24 percent to 29.13 percent.

**Zelio has appointed SEBI-registered Brickwork Ratings India as the monitoring agency to oversee the utilization of the proceeds raised through the issue.**

**The company stated that the capital infusion will support its nationwide expansion strategy, including the development of its upcoming electric three-wheeler manufacturing facility in Patan, Haryana.**

> “Our next phase is about building the capacity and market reach needed to serve a much larger customer base across India. The proposed fundraise will give us greater room to expand our manufacturing footprint, strengthen our distribution network and accelerate the development of our upcoming three-wheeler facility in Patan. We have built the business with a focus on profitable growth, and the priority now is to take that foundation into more markets while continuing to invest in the capabilities needed for scale,” **said Kunal Arya, Managing Director of Zelio E-Mobility.**

**The EV maker currently operates manufacturing facilities in Haryana, Odisha, and Tamil Nadu.** Earlier this year, the company inaugurated a new production facility in Coimbatore with an annual manufacturing and assembly capacity of 60,000 electric two-wheelers. **With the addition of the new plant, Zelio’s total installed production capacity has reached 2.4 lakh units annually.**

**The company currently works with over 400 dealers across more than 25 states and aims to expand its dealership network to over 550 outlets by the end of FY27.**

Alongside the fundraising proposal, shareholders will also vote on related-party transactions worth up to Rs 50 crore each with Torque Innovation EV Auto Private Limited, AVR Auto Industries Private Limited, Jai Bharat Engineering Tools, Jai Bharat Auto Components, and Rajdhani Machinery Store. **Zelio stated that these transactions, involving the purchase and sale of goods, will be undertaken in the ordinary course of business and on an arm’s-length basis.**

**Headquartered in Hisar, Haryana, Zelio manufactures electric two-wheelers under the Zelio brand and electric three-wheelers under the Tanga brand.**

For FY26, the company reported standalone revenue from operations of Rs 303.54 crore, reflecting a 76.28 percent increase from Rs 172.19 crore in the previous financial year. Standalone profit after tax rose 75.41 percent to Rs 28.03 crore from Rs 15.98 crore a year earlier.

Lab-grown diamond jewellery startup ONYA has secured Rs 12.5 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by Divisa Family Office, with existing investor Zeropearl VC increasing its commitment by participating again after the company’s earlier Rs 5.5 crore seed funding round.

**The round also builds on support from several angel investors who participated in the startup’s seed stage, including the founders of MyGate, the founder of UrbanVault, and other investors.**

According to the company, the newly raised capital will be used to strengthen its retail presence, drive digital customer acquisition, enhance online personalization capabilities, and expand research and development efforts focused on product innovation, design, and manufacturing.

Founded in 2024 by Gaurav Choudhary and Himani Yadav, ONYA is a lab-grown diamond jewellery brand that combines technology-driven diamond creation with contemporary jewellery design.

**Based in Bengaluru, the company offers IGI-certified lab-grown diamonds set in BIS Hallmarked gold, with a focus on personalized designs and craftsmanship.** The brand states that its products provide consumers with an alternative to natural diamonds at approximately 20 percent of the cost, while also offering a lifetime exchange and buyback program.

ONYA has also developed its proprietary ONYA Setting, a patented ring-setting design, along with its flagship ONYA Signature Collection, which draws inspiration from Neoclassical architecture.

**Since its launch, the company claims to have established a retail network of eight flagship stores across key locations in Bengaluru, Pune’s Amanora Gold Souk Mall, and Hyderabad’s Jubilee Hills.** The brand further stated that it has achieved monthly recurring revenue of Rs 3.5 crore.

Looking ahead, **ONYA plans to enter additional markets through a mix of company-owned outlets and franchise-led expansion.**

The startup operates in India’s growing lab-grown diamond jewellery segment, competing with brands such as Aukera, Limelight, Jewel Box, Fiona, and other players in the category.

**Investor interest in the segment has increased significantly in recent years.** According to industry data cited by the company, nine dedicated lab-grown diamond startups collectively raised $26.4 million in 2025, compared to $4.7 million in 2024.

The sector has witnessed several notable funding rounds, including Aukera’s Rs 90 crore debt raise in July following a $15 million equity round led by Peak XV Partners. Limelight Lab Grown Diamonds also secured Rs 275 crore in a strategic funding round to expand its manufacturing and retail operations, while GIVA, which operates the lab-grown diamond brand Heer, raised Rs 530 crore in a Series C funding round. Other funded companies in the space include Jewelbox, Lucira Jewellery, True Diamond, and Fiona Diamonds.

Quick commerce healthcare platform Rio Health has secured Rs 43.08 crore (approximately $4.5 million) in a pre-Series A funding round led by new investor Version One Ventures, with participation from existing backers Xeed Ventures, Good Capital, and Amplify Partner.

According to the company, **it currently processes more than 30,000 orders every month, with an average order value ranging between Rs 600 and Rs 700. Repeat customers account for nearly 80 percent of total orders.**

**Founded by Ankur Agrawal and Amit Ahuja, Rio Health operates a quick-commerce model for medicines and healthcare essentials, offering deliveries across Delhi NCR within 20 to 30 minutes**. The platform provides access to over 20,000 SKUs, while additional long-tail medicines are sourced through its distributor network.

Design-led lifestyle tech brand DailyObjects has appointed Zeenah Vilcassim as its Global Chief Marketing Officer (CMO), as the company strengthens its leadership team to support its international growth plans.

**With more than 17 years of experience across markets including the US, Europe, the Middle East, China, and India, Vilcassim brings expertise in brand building, consumer business growth, and market expansion.**

Preventive pain care startup betterhood has secured Rs 11.5 crore in a seed funding round led by Sauce, with participation from existing investor Kairon Capital.

**Earlier this year, the Bengaluru-based company had raised Rs 5 crore in the same funding round led by Kairon Capital.** The round also saw participation from Yogesh Kabra, Rishubh Satiya, Rohit Chawla, Sifat Khurana, and Shayamal Vallabhjee.

**The newly raised capital will be utilized to strengthen its product offerings, widen its presence across quick commerce and modern retail channels, and expand its content initiatives and physiotherapist network.**

Established in October 2024 by Vikram Kadam and Neha Zade, **betterhood focuses on preventive pain care solutions designed to address early symptoms of back, neck, and joint discomfort.**

**The brand offers a range of products including posture and ergonomic supports, orthotic soft goods such as back, knee, ankle, and wrist supports, as well as pain relief and recovery solutions.**

**The company said these product categories collectively account for an estimated Rs 20,000 crore market in India and continue to grow at a low- to mid-teen rate.**

As part of its ecosystem approach, betterhood has developed Physio Circle, a nationwide community dedicated to creating awareness around posture, movement, pain prevention, and recovery. The network currently includes more than 7,000 physiotherapists.

**The company has also introduced The Physio Edge, a certification program aimed at helping early-career physiotherapists bridge the gap between academic education and practical clinical experience.**

Since launching operations, **betterhood claims to have served more than 2 lakh customers and created over 1,500 educational content pieces across digital platforms focused on posture, movement, pain prevention, and recovery.**

**The preventive pain management segment has witnessed increased investor interest in recent years.** Nivaan Care raised $7 million to expand its non-surgical chronic pain management clinics, while Litemed’s CURAPOD secured Rs 20 crore in a pre-Series A funding round to scale its photobiomodulation-based wearable pain management technology. **Heatronics also raised Rs 1.8 crore to strengthen its preventive pain management and heat therapy device portfolio.**

**In 2025, Zanskar secured Rs 2.8 crore to broaden its pain care product range and invest in research and development for chronic pain and recovery solutions.** Meanwhile, Stance Health raised $1 million to advance its technology-driven musculoskeletal care platform, which integrates diagnosis, physiotherapy, and recovery programs.
