![{Funding Alert} DailyObjects Set to Raise Rs 350 Cr from Xponentia Capital and Anicut Capital](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-22T151628.857.jpg)

Lifestyle and tech accessories brand DailyObjects is reportedly in the final stages of securing a funding round worth approximately Rs 350 crore, with Xponentia Capital and Anicut Capital’s growth equity fund expected to lead the investment. **The transaction could value the Gurugram-based company at around Rs 1,000 crore.**

**The proposed round is expected to include a mix of primary and secondary share sales.** The fresh capital will likely be used to broaden DailyObjects’ product offerings, strengthen its distribution network, and support efforts to reach a larger customer base.

Founded in 2012 by Pankaj Garg and Saurav Adlakha, DailyObjects began as a design-led accessories brand focused on blending technology, utility, and aesthetics. Over the years, the company has expanded beyond smartphone accessories to build a wider portfolio that includes phone cases, laptop sleeves, smartwatch accessories, charging products, tech gadgets, organizers, bags, wallets, pouches, and workplace essentials.

**The brand has also increased its offline retail presence through exclusive stores, airport outlets, and partnerships with Apple Premium Retail locations.** According to reports, DailyObjects is now available across more than 250 retail locations spanning over 85 cities, including major metropolitan markets and airport retail hubs.

**The company has been investing in both product expansion and offline growth as it works toward scaling revenue and improving profitability.** Earlier this year, founder Pankaj Garg told CNBC-TV18 that DailyObjects expected to close FY26 with net revenue between Rs 215 crore and Rs 220 crore, while targeting revenue of Rs 400 crore in the current financial year. The anticipated growth is being driven by an expanding retail footprint and a broader product portfolio.

The upcoming funding round follows previous investments from firms including Seedfund, Unilazer Ventures, Roots Ventures, 360 One, and Trifecta Capital Advisors. **The company has raised approximately $14.5 million in funding to date.**

**DailyObjects was exploring a fundraise of around Rs 300 crore through a combination of primary and secondary transactions, with Xponentia Capital expected to lead the round.** The latest developments suggest that the size of the transaction has increased to approximately Rs 350 crore, with the inclusion of Anicut Capital’s growth equity fund.

![{Funding Alert} High-Protein Food Brand Protein Pantry Bags Rs 9 Cr Seed Funding Led by Sharrp Ventures ](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-22T105157.811.jpg)

Delhi-based high-protein frozen food brand Protein Pantry has secured Rs 9 crore in a seed funding round led by Sharrp Ventures, with participation from Peercheque, Consumer Collective by Atrium, and Indian Silicon Valley Capital. **The round also saw backing from angel investors including Varun Alagh, Rishubh Satiya, Avnish Anand, Arush Chopra, Saurabh Munjal, Signal Ventures, and others.**

**The newly raised capital will be used to strengthen its manufacturing capabilities, scale production, and support ongoing investments in research and development as well as supply chain operations.**

**Founded in November last year by Disha Bhattacharya and Prashanth Bhushan, Protein Pantry operates in the clean-label frozen food segment, offering high-protein, ready-to-cook products designed for Indian households.** The company said its products are made using kitchen-shelf ingredients and do not contain refined flour, preservatives, or palm oil. The brand follows a 1:10 protein-to-calorie ratio across its portfolio and manufactures all products in-house.

**Protein Pantry has expanded its direct-to-consumer presence across Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Jaipur.** The brand is also available on quick commerce platforms including Blinkit, FirstClub, and Flipkart Minutes in Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, and Hyderabad.

The company stated that it has served more than 30,000 households so far and recorded a strong repeat purchase rate. **It is planning to extend its quick commerce presence to Pune, Kolkata, Lucknow, Chandigarh, Ludhiana, and Chennai by the end of the year.**

**The brand is focused on addressing growing demand for protein-rich food options beyond traditional supplements and snack products.** Its current portfolio includes baked soya chaap, kebabs, cutlets, and falafels, all produced without refined flour, preservatives, or palm oil. Protein Pantry also develops its marinades, sauces, and chaap base at its own manufacturing facility.

**Looking ahead, the company plans to introduce new product formats and expand its protein-focused portfolio over the next 12 to 24 months.** It aims to strengthen its footprint across major Indian cities through both direct-to-consumer and quick commerce channels.

![{Funding Alert} Electric Mobility Startup Drivn Secures Rs 45 Cr from Avaana Capital](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-21T163439.677.jpg)

Electric commercial mobility startup Drivn has secured Rs 45 crore (approximately $4.7 million) in a seed funding round led by Avaana Capital, strengthening its efforts to build an integrated electric mobility platform for commercial transportation in India.

**The funding comes several months after the company announced an $80 million capital commitment from Japanese financial services firm Nomura in February 2026.** While that commitment was made at the group level, the latest investment has been raised by Drivn’s Indian operating entity. The company’s parent holding firm is headquartered in Singapore.

**The board of Drivn’s Indian entity approved the issuance of 33,98,792 compulsorily convertible preference shares (CCPS) at a price of Rs 132.40 per share.** Avaana Capital participated as the sole investor in the funding round, contributing the entire Rs 45 crore.

**The company plans to utilize the newly raised capital to support business expansion, operational requirements, and other general corporate purposes.**

**Founded in 2025 by Manav Bansal and Alpna Jain, Gurugram-based Drivn is focused on developing a full-stack electric mobility ecosystem for large commercial vehicles.** The startup operates in the electric transportation segment by owning and leasing electric intercity buses and heavy-duty trucks, while also providing fleet management and operational services to commercial fleet operators.

**Beyond vehicle deployment, Drivn offers charging infrastructure solutions and battery lifecycle management services, aiming to support businesses transitioning from conventional fleets to electric mobility.**

**Following the latest investment, Drivn Transition PTE. LTD, the Singapore-based parent company, continues to hold a majority stake of 88.75 percent in the Indian business.** Avaana Capital now owns 7.22 percent, while co-founder and Chief Executive Officer Manav Bansal holds 4.03 percent.

**Despite securing funding and attracting strategic backing, the Indian entity remained at a pre-revenue stage during FY26.** Regulatory filings show that the company reported a loss of Rs 1.96 crore during the financial year as it continued to invest in building its operations and platform capabilities.

**The latest funding underscores growing investor interest in the commercial electric vehicle ecosystem, particularly in areas such as fleet electrification, charging infrastructure, and integrated mobility services.**

![Ubalance Naturals Launches New Brand Identity Across Wellness Portfolio](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-21T152214.315.jpg)

Ayurvedic wellness brand Ubalance Naturals has introduced a new brand identity, ‘The Forest Within’, as part of its strategy to strengthen its presence in the premium wellness market. **The refreshed identity will be implemented across the company’s portfolio of nine products and 18 SKUs, while supporting its goal of achieving Rs 100 crore in revenue by FY30.**

**The rebranding initiative is inspired by the company’s systems-based approach to wellness, which emphasizes the interconnected nature of the body’s functions rather than treating individual concerns in isolation.** Beginning in September 2026, the new identity will be reflected across product packaging, digital channels, e-commerce platforms, and retail touchpoints.

**Ubalance Naturals develops wellness products that combine Ayurvedic formulations with wild-sourced botanicals.** The brand focuses on processing methods designed to preserve ingredient quality and offers liquid Ayurvedic formulations aimed at convenient consumption and effective nutrient absorption.

> **Gurmeet Kaur, Co-founder, Ubalance Naturals said,** *“Our customers have always trusted us for what’s inside the bottle. Now, the outside reflects the same authenticity and purpose. The Forest Within brings our philosophy of interconnected balance to life through a refined visual identity rooted in nature and true to who we have always been. Building on its established approach to wellness, Ubalance Naturals combines wild-sourced botanicals, careful processing to preserve ingredient integrity, and liquid Ayurvedic formulations designed for ease of consumption and efficient nutrient delivery. As the brand looks to the future, the rebrand will extend across packaging, digital platforms, e-commerce and retail touchpoints from September 2026, creating a cohesive premium experience that reflects the brand’s philosophy and ambitions. We are working towards a bold vision of expanding our reach to 100,000 families by 2028.”*

The company said the refreshed identity is intended to reinforce its positioning within the premium wellness category while creating a unified brand experience across customer touchpoints, including packaging, social media, digital platforms, e-commerce channels, and physical retail environments.

> **Devendra Kumar Oberoi, Co-founder, Ubalance Naturals added,** *“Our purpose has always been rooted in a simple belief: when the body and mind find balance, human potential flourishes. The Forest Within brings this philosophy to life, giving our belief in interconnected wellbeing a new expression inspired by nature. Our identity has evolved, but our purpose remains unchanged.”*

Alongside the brand refresh, Ubalance Naturals has outlined ambitious growth plans. **The company aims to expand its customer base to 100,000 families by 2028 while working towards its long-term revenue target of Rs 100 crore by FY30.**

**The rebranding reflects a broader effort by wellness brands to build stronger consumer connections through purpose-led storytelling, premium design, and consistent brand experiences across online and offline channels.** For Ubalance Naturals, the new identity is expected to support its next phase of growth while reinforcing its focus on holistic wellness rooted in Ayurveda and nature-inspired formulations.

 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

![{Funding Alert} Educational Toys Brand Skillmatics Explores Funding Round After FY26 Growth](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-21T132341.742.jpg)

Educational toys and learning games company Skillmatics is reportedly exploring a fresh funding round as it seeks to accelerate growth and expand its business operations. **The development comes after the company delivered strong revenue growth while maintaining profitability during FY26.**

**Skillmatics recorded Rs 659 crore in revenue from operations in FY26, reflecting a 34.5 percent increase from Rs 490 crore in FY25.**

**Founded as an educational and entertainment-focused brand, Skillmatics operates a direct-to-consumer (D2C) and omnichannel business catering to children aged one to 12 years.** The company offers a range of educational toys, activity kits, and learning games through its own digital platforms, online marketplaces, and retail partnerships.

**The Mumbai-headquartered company has established a significant international presence, with products available in over 25 countries and distributed through more than 3,000 retail stores worldwide.** North America continues to be its largest market and a key contributor to growth.

**International operations remained the primary revenue driver during FY26.** Approximately 87 percent of the company’s operating income was generated from markets outside India, largely through its US subsidiary, Grasper Global Inc. In addition to operating revenue, **Skillmatics earned Rs 7.52 crore through other income streams, taking its total revenue for the year to nearly Rs 667 crore, compared to Rs 496 crore in FY25.**

**Despite strong top-line growth, the company witnessed a significant increase in expenses.** Total expenditure rose by 36.1 percent year-on-year to Rs 652 crore in FY26, up from Rs 479 crore in the previous fiscal.

**Marketing continued to be one of the company's largest spending categories, accounting for nearly Rs 169 crore, or around 26 percent of overall expenditure.** Manufacturing costs related to toys and games stood at approximately Rs 130 crore, while packaging, logistics, commissions, employee benefits, and other operational expenses also contributed to the higher cost structure.

**As a result of rising costs, profit growth remained relatively moderate compared to revenue expansion.** Skillmatics reported a net profit of Rs 17.57 crore in FY26, up 4.2 percent from Rs 16.86 crore a year earlier.

**The company posted an EBITDA margin of 1.75 percent, while its return on capital employed (ROCE) stood at 5.14 percent during the fiscal year.**

On a unit economics basis, **Skillmatics spent nearly 99 paise to generate every rupee of operating revenue, highlighting the impact of marketing and expansion-related investments on profitability.**

**The company closed FY26 with current assets of around Rs 222 crore, including cash and bank balances of Rs 75.5 crore, providing a solid liquidity position as it prepares for its next phase of growth.**

Backed by investors including Peak XV Partners and Sofina, Skillmatics has raised approximately $28 million across multiple funding rounds.

LIMIRA Introduces Digital-First Lab-Grown Diamond Jewellery Brand in India

![Indian Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/art-logo.webp)

BY - [Indian Retailer Bureau](/author/indian-retailer-bureau)  
 Sub Editor  / 1 MIN READ

[Follow Us ![Indina Retailer](https://www.indianretailer.com/themes/custom/menshealth/images/follow.webp)](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAiEJjETmBVGGR4AF2qcS42jEMqFAgKIhCYxE5gVRhkeABdqnEuNoxD?hl=en-IN&gl=IN&ceid=IN%3Aen)

![LIMIRA Introduces Digital-First Lab-Grown Diamond Jewellery Brand in India](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-21T112348.141.jpg)

LIMIRA, a newly launched lab-grown diamond jewellery brand, has entered the Indian market with an e-commerce-only business model focused on design, self-expression, and transparency. **The brand aims to offer consumers a digital-first jewellery shopping experience, catering to changing buying habits as more customers research and purchase jewellery online.**

**The launch comes as India's diamond jewellery sector continues to expand.** According to the 2025 De Beers India Diamond Acquisition Study, India now accounts for 12 percent of global diamond jewellery demand, up from 10 percent in 2019, making it the world's second-largest diamond jewellery market.

**At the core of LIMIRA's approach is a gender-neutral design philosophy that encourages consumers to choose jewellery based on personal preferences rather than traditional gender-based classifications.** The brand's positioning is reflected in its tagline, **“Not His, Not Hers, Just Yours.”**

**LIMIRA has introduced four debut collections—****Orbit, Fortuna, Ember, and Eterne****—each centred around a unique narrative.** Orbit celebrates the connection between sisters and close female friendships, while Fortuna reinterprets the horseshoe as a symbol of luck and opportunity. Ember is inspired by meaningful moments and individual expression, and Eterne highlights enduring relationships, memories, and experiences. Through these collections, the brand seeks to position jewellery as a reflection of everyday emotions and personal stories, rather than only major life milestones.

The collection features lab-grown diamond jewellery crafted in 9KT and 14KT gold, available in rose gold, yellow gold, and white gold options. By operating without a physical retail footprint, LIMIRA is placing online discovery and shopping at the centre of its customer journey.

> **Rashmi Gajera, CEO, LIMIRA** said, *“We believe diamonds should not be reserved only for milestones and celebrations. They can be part of an individual’s everyday signature, reflecting who they are, how they feel and how they choose to express themselves. LIMIRA was created to rethink not only the jewellery itself, but the experience of discovering and buying it. Our e-commerce-only model allows us to put design, individuality and transparency at the centre of that experience, while lab-grown diamonds open up new possibilities for how consumers engage with diamond jewellery.”*

**The brand's launch aligns with changing consumer preferences, as jewellery buyers increasingly look for products that resonate with their personal identity, style, and values.** Industry trends indicate that jewellery is becoming less tied to traditional occasions and more integrated into everyday fashion and self-expression.

As India's consumer market continues to evolve, LIMIRA is positioning itself to serve a growing segment of shoppers seeking design-led, accessible, and digitally enabled diamond jewellery experiences.

Digital physiotherapy platform Physioplus Healthcare has raised a strategic seed investment from HBF India at a valuation of $800,000, as the company looks to strengthen its technology capabilities and broaden its footprint across the country.

According to the company, **the fresh capital will be used to enhance its technology platform, expand its professional network, and increase its presence in multiple markets across India.**

**Founded in 2022 by Samit Saxena, Jaswant Singh, and Madhukar Pareek, Physioplus Healthcare enables patients to connect with certified physiotherapists through a digital platform.** The company offers services including physiotherapy discovery, virtual consultations, patient assessments, clinical documentation, and technology-driven monitoring.

**The startup said its platform integrates digital practice management tools, patient records, and remote monitoring capabilities to support physiotherapy treatment and rehabilitation programs.** Its offerings cater to a range of health concerns, including chronic pain, musculoskeletal disorders, sports injuries, and post-operative recovery.

**Physioplus operates in the growing digital healthcare and physiotherapy segment, where several startups are leveraging technology to improve access to rehabilitation services.** Last year, FlexifyMe raised $2.4 million in a pre-Series A funding round led by IvyCap Ventures and Signal Ventures to scale its online physiotherapy platform.

**Meanwhile, Stance Health secured $1 million in pre-seed funding in 2025 to expand its technology-enabled musculoskeletal care model, while Rebee Health attracted investment from 1337 Ventures in 2025 to grow its wearable sensor-based digital physiotherapy platform.**

With the latest funding, Physioplus Healthcare plans to further develop its digital infrastructure and strengthen its position in India’s evolving physiotherapy and rehabilitation technology market.

The investment comes just months after the company’s launch. **According to MoroMaa, two of its products sold out within the first two months of operations, reflecting early consumer interest in the brand’s offerings.**

**The newly raised capital will be used to expand the company’s product range, strengthen its distribution network, and increase market reach across India.**

Moufakir, who serves as the founder and chief executive officer of MoroMaa, brings experience from the finance and entertainment sectors. Under her leadership, the brand has focused on combining Moroccan ingredients, beauty traditions, and artistic influences in its product portfolio.

**With the fresh funding, MoroMaa plans to accelerate product innovation, widen distribution channels, and build greater awareness of Moroccan-inspired beauty products among Indian consumers.**

![{Funding Alert} Baby Essentials Startup Kiddo Raises Rs 12.5 Cr, Eyes Delhi NCR Expansion ](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-18T111723.673.jpg)

Baby-focused quick commerce startup Kiddo has secured Rs 12.5 crore in a pre-seed funding round led by Campus Fund, with participation from several strategic angel investors. **The capital will be deployed toward customer acquisition, expansion of its dark store network across Delhi NCR, technology and product development, and strengthening its team.**

Founded last year by Ankit Kawatra, **Kiddo operates in the baby care and parenting essentials segment, offering rapid delivery services alongside life-stage-based product recommendations tailored for parents.**

Industry estimates indicate that India’s baby care market was valued at $31 billion in 2022 and is expected to grow to $56 billion by 2029, supported by a compound annual growth rate of 13 percent to 14 percent.

**Since its launch, Kiddo says it has built a catalogue of more than 30,000 SKUs spanning baby essentials, fashion, and related categories.** The company currently serves customers in Delhi NCR, focusing on premium households, and plans to further expand its dark store footprint by the end of the year. It also states that its blended gross margins exceed those typically seen among horizontal grocery quick commerce platforms.

**The startup operates in a competitive market alongside players such as FirstCry, AllThingsBaby, and OZi, which are targeting the growing baby and kids' commerce space.**

Gurugram-based OZi raised $3.3 million in seed funding from Blume Ventures in October last year and later secured $6.2 million in a Series A round led by RTP Global in March this year. The platform offers more than 15,000 products and promises delivery within 60 minutes.

Another player, Bengaluru-based Peeko, raised $3.2 million from Stellaris Venture Partners in August last year before closing a Series A round worth Rs 67.4 crore led by Chiratae Ventures in August 2026. Peeko's portfolio includes baby apparel, toys, gear, and consumables.

**The baby commerce sector is also witnessing increased activity from established companies.** FirstCry, for instance, has been accelerating its faster-delivery initiatives as demand for convenience-led parenting solutions continues to rise across India.

![{Funding Alert} Sustainable Home Care Brand Ecosys Raises Funding for Next Growth Phase](https://indian-retailer.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/s3fs-public/2026-09/Untitled%20design%20-%202026-09-17T142954.493.jpg)

Ecosys, a laundry and home cleaning products startup, has secured Rs 5 crore in a pre-Series A funding round led by GVFL Prarambh Fund, with participation from Proteus Partners, which is backed by operator-investors Puru Gupta and Sreejith Moolayil.

**With this investment, the Mumbai-based company’s total funding raised to date has reached Rs 7.94 crore.**

**The fresh capital will be utilized to strengthen brand awareness, expand consumer reach through digital channels, and introduce new product formats across the laundry and home-cleaning categories.**

**Founded in 2017 by Sumit Goyal and Chirag Dangi, Ecosys develops eco-friendly cleaning solutions with a focus on reducing plastic waste.** The company is known for its sustainable laundry and cleaning pods, which use 10 ml polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) capsules that dissolve completely in water, eliminating the need for conventional single-use plastic packaging.

**The startup offers a range of household cleaning products, including laundry detergent pods, floor cleaners, glass cleaners, bathroom cleaners, and kitchen and utensil cleaning sprays.** Its formulations are designed to be biodegradable, non-toxic, and suitable for households with children and pets.

**The company operates in a rapidly growing market.** Industry estimates suggest that India’s household cleaning products sector is expanding at an annual rate of nearly 14 percent, significantly outpacing the global average growth rate.

Ecosys positions itself as a premium and convenience-driven brand, distributing its products through e-commerce and quick-commerce platforms to reach urban consumers seeking sustainable cleaning alternatives.

**The funding comes at a time when India’s home-care and laundry startup ecosystem is witnessing increased demand for environmentally conscious products, including laundry pods, refill solutions, plant-based cleaners, concentrated formulations, and low-waste packaging formats.**

**Several startups in the segment have attracted investor interest in recent years.** Home-cleaning brand Koparo raised Rs 14.5 crore in an extended pre-Series A funding round last year, while Cleevo secured $1 million in seed funding. Sustainable home and personal care brand Beco raised $10 million from Tanglin Venture Partners, and Scrubsy recently secured Rs 27 crore from V3 Ventures in August this year.

Luxury hair extensions and wig brand Hair Originals has secured $1.25 million led by Anicut Capital, Kesh Kala Family Office, JITO Angel Network, Lets Venture, Dexter Angels, Pankaj Chaddah, and Ahana Gupta. Dexter Capital acted as the exclusive advisor for Hair Originals.

Earlier, Hair Originals had raised Rs 60 lacs from three investors at the show Shark Tank. The company has also raised Rs 30 crore early this year in the pre-seed funding round, where it received angel investments from marquee investors.

Hair Originals plans to utilise the raised funds to scale their business operations by 4X, achieve 100 crore ARR by the end of 2024, expand to 25 cities across India with experience centres in 5 major cities and to introduce their direct to consumer services in the US market, Hair Originals said in a press release.

Founded in 2019, the company currently exports its products to over 22 countries, including top luxury salons across the US, Europe, and Africa.

Launched in 2019, Hair Originals operates a hair extension and wigs platform. Hair Originals operates in about 20 cities in the country. # Hair Originals on a mission to scale business post Shark Tank India appearance

## In a recent conversation with YourStory’s Daily Dispatch powered by HSBC, Jitendra Sharma, Founder, Hair Originals talks about the company’s ambitious growth plans.

![Photo of Suryatapa Chakraborty](https://images.yourstory.com/cs/users/40f5f790-c39f-11eb-ab0b-1583f8394132/profile_image_1624379370921.jpeg?format=auto&w=96&q=75)
![Hair Originals on a mission to scale business post Shark Tank India appearance ](https://images.yourstory.com/cs/2/40f5f790c39f11ebab0b1583f8394132/JitendraSharma-800x400-1643877251924.png?mode=crop&crop=faces&ar=2%3A1&format=auto&w=1920&q=75)

Friday February 04, 2022 , 2 min Read

![Google Preferred](https://images.yourstory.com/assets/images/google_preferred.webp?format=auto&w=384&q=75)

Gurugram-based hair extension and wigs brand ﻿Hair Original﻿ has raised about **$30 million** from marquee investors after appearing in the popular business reality show Shark Tank India.

Speaking about the fundraise, **Jitendra Sharma, Founder, Hair Originals** shares that since the startup is dealing with a very unique product —  human hair extensions — the funding received can provide validation for the idea.

Hair Originals will use the fresh capital to ramp up its supply chain and production capacity. Apart from that, it will educate people via different forms of marketing, especially those suffering from hair loss.

![Hair Originals ](https://images.yourstory.com/cs/2/40f5f790c39f11ebab0b1583f8394132/JitendraSharma-1643877424753.jpeg?fm=png&auto=format&w=800&blur=500)

Jitendra Sharma, Founder, Hair Originals

### ALSO READ

![NARCL, IDRCL ready to commence ops: SBI Chairman](https://images.yourstory.com/cs/2/f86c090087cc11eba777b34f5b721f5e/Photo-DineshKumarKhara-1643361307474.png?fm=png&auto=format&h=100&w=100&crop=entropy&fit=crop)

Jitendra mentions that Hair Originals operates in about **20 cities** in the country. Within the next 15 months, it plans to reach **50 cities** and hopes to fulfil a revenue target of **Rs 100 crore**.

He adds that the startup’s objective is to eventually make the entire process online. It currently has two board product categories — DIY hair extensions which can be bought from their online store and permanent hair extension that requires the assistance of a salon or a stylist.

“We are onboarding many salon partners in different cities so that any consumer sitting in any city in India can buy the products and get free installations,” he says.

Commenting on the sourcing and manufacturing part of the process, Jitendra shares that the company sources hair from the southern part of India, primarily temples. In terms of manufacturing units, Hair Originals started with Indore and has opened another manufacturing capacity in Gurgaon. It now wishes to move towards other smaller cities as well.

Lastly, in terms of future roadmaps, he says that apart from focusing on India market, Hair Originals plans to soon launch its business in the US.
